about.text: A spontaneously fermented raw milk of Zambia, left at room temperature in a calabash for about two days. Lactococcus dominates, and seven named types are known, e.g. tonga and barotse.

facts.v: Named after Barotseland, the old name of Zambia's Western province, where most is made; whey is drained from the calabash between additions of fresh raw milk, over four to seven days
A type in which part of each batch is kept as the starter for the next, repeated over many cycles
